clue.text: Bank accepting support is failing

indicators.note: a bank that accepts something takes it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a bank of earth is a mound
a rib is a supporting member, as in a boat or vault

explanation.surface: A bank that takes in a backer is clearly in trouble and about to fold.
explanation.definitionFit: Something moribund is in terminal decline, close to death or collapse.

clue.text: Radio report's failed to notice obscurity

indicators.note: a radio report is heard rather than read, so the word goes by its spoken sound

parts.note: to have missed something is to have failed to notice it

explanation.surface: A radio bulletin overlooked something obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist is haze that obscures sight, so it stands for obscurity.

clue.text: Red Guard initially abandoning sport

indicators.note: abandoning says a letter is dropped from the sport

parts.note: rugby is a sport

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word Guard

explanation.surface: A Red Guard gives up a sport early on, a scene from China's Cultural Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Guard' reads as one phrase; 'Red' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby is a deep red colour, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Somehow a cable is absorbing temperature in marine environment

indicators.note: absorbing means the jumbled letters take another inside them
somehow suggests the letters are put together in some unstated order

explanation.surface: A submarine cable soaks up heat from the sea around it.
explanation.walkthrough: CABLEIS is rearranged into BALICSE, which takes T inside; the clue's 'a', put first in the surface, closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic Sea is a northern European sea, an example of a marine environment.

clue.text: Holy woman recording it is involving German with part of evening service

parts.note: a nun is a woman in a religious order
a CD is a compact disc recording

indicators.note: involving means the it is letters wrap round the German word

parts.note: mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A nun's recording, featuring German, is part of Evensong.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nunc Dimittis, Simeon's song, is a canticle sung at Evensong and Compline.

clue.text: Charlie not wanting two servings of energy drink

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to be off something, like your food, is to not want it
E is the physics symbol for energy, served twice over

explanation.surface: Someone named Charlie turns down a double helping of an energy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee is a common hot beverage brewed from roasted beans.

clue.text: Broadcasting revolutionary extract of Hungarian opera

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
extract of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rebellious excerpt from a Hungarian opera goes out over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being transmitted live.

clue.text: Protocol over occupying uniform part of track for racing

parts.note: form is correct procedure or protocol, as in good form
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: occupying means the over letter sits within the track part

parts.note: a lane is one division of a running track
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Rules about uniforms on part of a racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Formula One is the top class of international motor racing.

clue.text: Expect to lose half printing speed

indicators.note: losing half keeps only the opening three letters of the word Expect

parts.note: an edition is a single printing of a book

explanation.surface: Anticipate printing being done at half the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition is an old sense of promptness or haste, as in expeditious.

clue.text: Is taken aback a small amount about network making hissing sound

indicators.note: taken aback is read literally as turned back, so the word is reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning

indicators.note: about means one word sits around the other

parts.note: a bit is a small amount
LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: Someone surprised by a tiny amount of network coverage hisses in annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise, but it turns the word round; 'about' signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sibilant describes speech sounds like s and sh, which hiss.

clue.text: Brooded, putting blame on tyrant

parts.note: a hen that broods sits on eggs, so brooded is sat
to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Someone sulked, then pinned the blame on a despot.
explanation.definitionFit: A satrap was a Persian provincial governor, and by extension any despotic subordinate ruler.

clue.text: One right, say, to retire, with church living no longer very profitable

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals
say means for example, EG
quick once meant living, as in the quick and the dead; no longer marks the old sense

explanation.surface: A clergyman retires from the church, his living gone, and turns to easy money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' turns IRTEG into GETRI. A church living is a vicar's post, misleading here.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-rich-quick scheme promises fast large returns.

clue.text: Democrats in race, worn down, offering compromise position

indicators.note: in means the Democrats sit inside the race

parts.note: the mile is a classic running race
D is an abbreviation for Democrat; two of them make DD
something worn down is ground, as by a grindstone

explanation.surface: Democrats, exhausted by a contest, settle for a compromise.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural Democrats gives two Ds, put 'in' MILE.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle ground is the area of agreement between opposing views.

clue.text: Whence meat juices flow in disorderly manner

definitions.meaning: read literally, juices flow out of a joint of meat

explanation.surface: Where a roast's juices run, and how things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A dislocated bone is out of joint; figuratively, things in disarray are too.

clue.text: Flourishing iris loving fresh earth

indicators.note: flourishing as a showy wave or swirl signals the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: A thriving iris thrives in newly turned ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin soil is land never before cultivated, so it is untouched ground.

clue.text: Whole parts of African city with time regressing

indicators.note: regressing means the time letter goes back, further along the word

parts.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia

explanation.surface: Sections of a North African city are seen going back in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressing' moves the T of TUNIS back to before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Units are complete single things that together make up larger wholes.

clue.text: Month exactly right to host second parade

parts.note: March is a month

indicators.note: to host something is to hold it inside, so one word takes the letter in

parts.note: pat means exactly right, as in an answer off pat

explanation.surface: A month is just the right time to hold a second parade.
explanation.definitionFit: A march past is a ceremonial parade of troops filing past a saluting point.

clue.text: Sound conclusion, mostly, about vulgar festival

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go around the vulgar word

parts.note: sound in health means hale
low means vulgar or coarse

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A rowdy festival nearly reaches a healthy conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise but means healthy; 'mostly' trims the last letter and 'about' wraps the outer pieces round the vulgar word.
explanation.definitionFit: Halloween, the eve of All Saints' Day, is an annual festival on 31 October.

clue.text: Old cigar — it's unusually immoderate

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters come in an unusual order

explanation.surface: An old cigar is, surprisingly, excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Orgiastic means given to wild, unrestrained indulgence.

clue.text: Left bar, ignoring last of indecent language

indicators.note: ignoring says a letter is left out of the bar

parts.note: an ingot is a bar of metal

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word indecent

explanation.surface: Someone walks out of a bar, steering clear of crude talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops the T (last of indecent) from INGOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal slang for a language or jargon.

clue.text: Queen is as nothing I suspect, after jack's special quality

indicators.note: after places the scrambled letters behind the jack letter

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious, signalling the letters are not in true order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A card player reckons the queen counts for nothing next to the jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges QUEENISAS into ENESAISQU; 'after' puts it behind J, with O and I to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A je ne sais quoi is an indefinable appeal, a quality hard to put into words.

clue.text: Take control of French square

definitions.meaning: French for sixteen, the square of four

explanation.surface: Commandeer a square in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Seize means grab power; in French it is the number sixteen, four squared.

clue.text: Environment Agency upset about MPs heading off for recess

indicators.note: about means the turned letters wrap round the others
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters read back

parts.note: EA abbreviates the Environment Agency, a UK government body

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

explanation.surface: A government agency is upset with MPs going off on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives AE; 'heading off' strips M from MPs to leave PS. The Environment Agency is England's environmental regulator.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a recess, usually semicircular, at the end of a church.

clue.text: Lifted slates without much notice

indicators.note: lifted in a down clue means raised up, so the letters read from bottom up

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, as does one who pans

explanation.surface: Roof slates were raised at short notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap decision or election is one made suddenly, at little notice.

clue.text: One cricket club hosting cricket side I considered very special

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals

indicators.note: hosting means the club holds the following letters inside

parts.note: the on side is one half of a cricket field, the leg side

explanation.surface: A cricketer thinks his club taking on a particular side is a big occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the field divides into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is widely regarded as outstanding and emblematic.

clue.text: With no clear candidate emerging, success involves info about European

indicators.note: involves means the win wraps round what follows

parts.note: a win is a success

indicators.note: about means the info word goes around the European letter

parts.note: dope is slang for information

explanation.surface: An election with no front runner, where winning depends on intelligence about Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-open contest is one where any competitor might win.

clue.text: One directs roofer to add extra line

indicators.note: add extra signals a letter slipped in as an additional one

parts.note: a tiler lays roof tiles

explanation.surface: Someone tells a roofer to put in one more row of tiles.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiller is the lever that steers a boat, so it directs the vessel.

clue.text: Recognise power draws in sort without real engagement

indicators.note: draws in means the outer letters pull another word inside

parts.note: to see something is to recognise it
a kind is a sort

explanation.surface: Someone sees that power pulls in a certain type of person who never truly commits.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin-deep means superficial, not going beyond the surface.
